acceptance_criteria: Structured multi-agent final review remains available as an advisory MCP service without claiming Codex runtime authority.
Lifecycle and final-review coordination tools are exposed from the installed plugin root.
Editor, runner, repository-local, repository-remote, and diagnostics mutation capabilities remain unavailable from the plugin-wide surface.
All release artifacts, manifests, tests, and documentation describe and ship the same advisory surface.
Signed Tiber and Development Workflow EventCore commits retain the configured Git author and committer identity required by repository signature policy.
explicit_concerns: Do not restore unsupported Codex boundary enforcement.
Do not expose project mutation tools.
Review the public MCP behavior, source-to-binary parity, versioning, and installed-root startup.
Verify the Git-backed coordinator can publish signed transitions under GitHub verified-signature branch rules.
context.user_request: Restore the structured multi-agent review process that was unintentionally removed from the reduced bootstrap plugin while keeping the plugin advisory and withholding project mutation tools.

shared_test_evidence.summary: Strict Clippy passed; 344 coordinator and all 21 capability tests passed serially; the complete Tiber Rust suite and signed EventCore identity contracts passed; source-to-release parity and release completeness passed; all eight cross-harness MCP startup tests passed. The repository pre-commit gate passed before the final focused advisory metadata fix, whose complete affected Rust and startup gates then passed.

lens_objectives.agent-instruction-quality: Review whether plugin, skill, and MCP instructions accurately preserve the structured multi-agent workflow without claiming unsupported authority.
lens_objectives.architecture-maintainability: Identify evidence-backed failure modes caused by incoherent ownership boundaries, unsafe coupling, or complexity that makes the changed behavior difficult to modify or verify; do not report style preferences alone.
lens_objectives.correctness-behavior: Verify functional correctness, edge cases, state transitions, and behavioral regressions.
lens_objectives.operability-user-impact: Check runtime failure handling, diagnostics, operator impact, usability for changed user-facing behavior, and accessibility for changed interactive surfaces.
lens_objectives.production-risk-footguns: Identify production-scale failure modes such as resource exhaustion, unbounded retries or cardinality, unsafe defaults, burst behavior, and excessive data access.
lens_objectives.release-integration: Check only versioning, compatibility, packaging, documentation, CI, rollout, and downstream-integration obligations implied by the changed release surface.
lens_objectives.safety-human-harm: Identify plausible failures that could harm people or the physical world in the system's intended deployment.
lens_objectives.security-safety: Identify unauthorized-access, protected-data, trust-boundary, integrity, and abuse-resistance regressions introduced by the change.
lens_objectives.tests-verification: Assess whether tests and verification evidence cover the changed behavior and plausible failure modes.

subagent_lifecycle.policy: Start a fresh lens subagent for every review iteration and lens. Carry continuity only through this MCP state, prior defenses, and caller decisions. Close each assigned subagent after its result is collected.

dimensions.evidence: plugins/development-system/components/development-discipline/rust/src/main.rs changes the default dispatcher surface from plugin-read-only to plugin-advisory, admits all current workflow.* and final_review.* calls, and rewrites their advertised schemas and descriptions before tools/list returns them. The shared evidence reports the complete Development Discipline Rust and startup suites passing for diff 5488676d2a8c36fe0c68d4a6a3b2448f2692974d.
dimensions.material_impact: The restored structured review workflow could fail in normal use or violate the promised advisory-only capability boundary.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A filtering, dispatch, or description-rewrite mismatch could advertise a coordination call that is denied or semantically altered at invocation, or could expose a non-advisory capability under an admitted namespace.

dimensions.evidence: The supplied shared evidence is bound to the pinned diff hash and reports strict Clippy, 344 coordinator tests, 21 capability tests, complete Tiber tests, signed EventCore identity contracts, source-to-release parity, release completeness, eight cross-harness startup tests, and the repository pre-commit gate. Its summary also says pre-commit preceded a final focused advisory metadata fix and that the complete affected Rust and startup gates were rerun afterward.
dimensions.material_impact: A manifest, documentation, or formatting mismatch could ship despite the otherwise comprehensive behavior evidence.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A metadata-only regression outside the focused post-fix Rust and startup gates could remain even though the behavior and release-parity evidence is broad.

dimensions.evidence: ServiceSurface::PluginAdvisory explicitly admits reader/setup tools plus workflow.* and final_review.* while excluding workspace-editor.*, project-runner.*, repository-local.*, repository-remote.*, and system-diagnostics.*; dispatch checks service_surface.allows(name) before any semantic call. Capability and startup tests assert that only the intended namespaces are listed.
dimensions.material_impact: A later tool addition could silently widen the installed plugin's trust boundary and permit unintended local effects.
dimensions.plausible_failure: The namespace-prefix allow rule could admit a future workflow.* or final_review.* operation whose effects exceed advisory state coordination without requiring an explicit update to this surface.

dimensions.evidence: The intended deployment is a local single-owner developer plugin coordinating review and Git-backed task state; the diff adds no control of physical systems, medical decisions, safety-critical operations, or other plausible human-harm path.

The change reuses the existing WorkflowCore implementation through a new filtered PluginAdvisory surface, but the public boundary is expressed by namespace-prefix admission and advisory semantics are expressed by recursive text replacement over generated tool metadata.
dimensions.material_impact: Maintainers could unintentionally broaden the plugin surface or reintroduce runtime-authority claims during otherwise local coordinator changes.
dimensions.plausible_failure: Future coordination tools or wording changes could drift past the prefix filter or replacement table, leaving public behavior and advisory messaging inconsistent with the underlying shared coordinator.

dimensions.evidence: Top-level Claude and Codex MCP manifests, the component manifest, launch arguments, READMEs, and startup tests all move from plugin-read-only to plugin-advisory. The dispatcher now rejects stale or non-Unicode DEVELOPMENT_SYSTEM_SERVICE values instead of silently selecting the former default, and tests require an actionable failure for the stale service name.
dimensions.material_impact: Affected users lose the Development Discipline MCP surface until they update the stale registration or reinstall the plugin.
dimensions.plausible_failure: An installation that retains an old launcher argument or DEVELOPMENT_SYSTEM_SERVICE=plugin-read-only will fail to start after the binary upgrade, while an installed-root path or platform artifact mismatch would prevent all restored coordination tools from loading.

dimensions.evidence: The patch bumps the marketplace and top-level plugin to 5.0.2, the Development Discipline component to 0.19.2, and the Tiber component to 0.20.1; it replaces four Development Discipline platform binaries and one Tiber binary together with fingerprints and SHA-256 manifests. Shared evidence reports source-to-release parity, release completeness, and cross-harness installed-root startup passing.
dimensions.material_impact: The advisory review surface or signed-identity fix could be absent or fail at startup for a supported installation target.
dimensions.plausible_failure: Any stale binary, checksum, version, or harness manifest would make one platform or harness ship behavior different from the reviewed source and documentation.

dimensions.evidence: plugins/development-system/components/tiber/rust/crates/tiber-git/src/git_event_store.rs removes the hard-coded EventCore author and committer environment and lets git commit-tree resolve the repository's effective identity; signing remains conditional on commit.gpgsign. The contract tests cover configured identity and a signed authoritative branch.
dimensions.material_impact: Tiber and Development Workflow state transitions can be blocked from publication, leaving task and lifecycle coordination unavailable until Git identity or signing configuration is corrected.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A repository with missing, stale, or unexpectedly environment-overridden Git identity or signing configuration can fail EventCore publication or produce a signed commit whose attribution does not satisfy GitHub's repository policy.

dimensions.evidence: Initialization instructions and every exposed workflow/final-review tool description receive advisory framing, while README text says these records do not establish agent identity, execute project mutations, restrict ordinary tools, or authorize external actions. The implementation obtains that framing by recursively replacing a bounded set of authority phrases in shared tool metadata.
dimensions.material_impact: An agent could incorrectly claim lifecycle enforcement, skip an independent permission check, or misrepresent readiness despite the plugin being advisory only.
dimensions.plausible_failure: Unrewritten authority or gating language in a tool result, error, skill instruction, or newly added description could lead an agent to treat coordinator state as actual Codex capability enforcement or user authorization.

plan_assumptions: The supplied baseline commit, changed-file inventory, diff hash, and shared test evidence identify the complete review snapshot and are not re-resolved against a movable base.

The deployment is a local single-owner development tool; the repository, installed toolchain, PATH, environment, Git configuration, and owner are trusted, while ordinary misconfiguration, crashes, stale installation state, and remote publication failure remain in scope.

The advisory-surface restoration and Git identity correction can be verified and shipped coherently as one development-system patch release; they do not create a new independently owned runtime or delivery subsystem.

The supplied shared test evidence is the sole broad execution evidence for this scout; bundled binaries are assessed through its reported source-parity, checksum, release-completeness, and startup results rather than by running or reverse-engineering them here.
